evidence_sources_used: structured_agent_outputs.json (claim/evidence text, factors tag as secondary corroboration only, entities, agent, assertion_status)
evidence_sources_explicitly_not_used: evidence_stance_audit.json (B1 target-alpha stance -- avoided out of maximal anti-circularity caution)
method.direction: UNDERLYING EVIDENCE -> GOLD EVIDENCE CONDITION -> PRESENT/ABSENT/UNCERTAIN (never the reverse)
method.evidence_strength_note: evidence_strength reflects the strength of the EVIDENCE BASE informing the trigger_state call, whichever direction it points -- e.g. an ABSENT call backed by strong, explicit contrary evidence (such as QQQ-A001's 93% no-cut probability) is reported as evidence_strength=STRONG, not merely 'no evidence found'.

rules.evidence_condition: Current NVDA-specific evidence materially describes AI training/compute/GPU accelerator demand growth.
rules.evidence_summary: 'AI demand is exceptional' (HPE CEO framing, cited in NVDA sentiment coverage); 'AI demand supercycle narrative' (Broadcom CEO $230B 2028 AI revenue projection cited as reinforcing NVDA's own thesis); the $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition explicitly framed as NVDA expanding across the AI stack.
rules.trigger_rationale: Multiple independent agents (sentiment_agent, news_agent) report concrete, dated, NVDA-attributed AI-demand evidence with no contrary signal found.

rules.evidence_condition: Current NVDA-specific evidence supports company revenue growth, raised guidance, or fundamental demand-driven revenue transmission.
rules.evidence_summary: 'Revenue, EPS, and FCF are all accelerating, with Q1 FY27 delivering 85% YoY revenue growth and record FCF of $48.6B'; '63.7% net margin' -- concrete, quantified company-specific fundamental data from fundamental_agent (Primary), corroborated by bull_researcher and research_manager summaries of the same underlying data.
rules.trigger_rationale: Concrete quantified revenue/margin/FCF figures from a Primary fundamental source -- not inferred from AI-leader identity.

rules.evidence_condition: Current NVDA-specific evidence materially supports valuation compression, rich valuation, or multiple downside risk.
rules.evidence_summary: 'NVDA at 8% of S&P 500 market cap and "priced for perfection" concerns'; 'the market is demanding perfection and punishing any [stumble]' (peer AVGO/HPE cited as cautionary precedent for NVDA's own richly-valued position); 'rising rate-hike odds pressuring high-multiple tech.'
rules.trigger_rationale: Direct NVDA-attributed valuation-concentration framing plus closely analogous peer precedent explicitly linked to NVDA's own risk profile.

rules.evidence_condition: Both a supported growth side (A101 and/or A301) and a supported valuation-risk side (A304) present in the same run.
rules.evidence_summary: Both legs of the composite are independently PRESENT/STRONG (see NVDA-A101-AI-GROWTH, NVDA-A301-FUNDAMENTAL-GROWTH, NVDA-A304-VALUATION-RISK above).
rules.trigger_rationale: Growth side triggered by BOTH AI growth (A101) and fundamental growth (A301) independently; valuation-risk side (A304) also independently present. This evidence-side finding does NOT inspect or assert anything about the actual admitted conflict -- that is Step 4.

rules.evidence_condition: Current NVDA-specific evidence supports AI infrastructure buildout (A103), semiconductor-cycle conditions (A201), and/or narrative/momentum dynamics (A601).
rules.evidence_summary: A103 (AI Infrastructure): PRESENT/MODERATE -- 'AI infrastructure demand environment... exceptional, red-hot, constrained by supply' (peer-sourced, CLEAR_TRANSMISSION to NVDA as supplier); fundamental_agent: 'Any slowdown in AI infrastructure spending would directly pressure revenue' (DIRECT_TICKER). A201 (Semiconductor Supercycle): UNCERTAIN -- evidence found (inventory build $5.3B->$25.8B, low capex intensity, TSMC fab reliance) is company-specific supply-chain/balance-sheet detail, not a clean industry-wide inventory/ASP/order-cycle recovery signal distinct from NVDA's own AI-demand story. A601 (Narrative Momentum): PRESENT/STRONG -- 'the Hugging Face acquisition is the dominant narrative'; 'retail is actively discussing the Hugging Face deal... retail is aligned with upside' (DIRECT_TICKER; unrelated MACD/RSI technical-momentum false-matches excluded).
rules.trigger_rationale: Rule-level state is PRESENT because 2 of 3 supporting concepts (A103, A601) are independently present with real evidence; A201 specifically remains UNCERTAIN. This rule is non-mandatory regardless of outcome.

rules.evidence_condition: Current macro evidence relevant to QQQ's constituent basis supports falling-rate/easing/discount-rate-relief transmission.
rules.evidence_summary: '93% probability of NO Fed rate cuts in 2026 (up +4.3pp over the week)'; '72% probability of a Fed rate HIKE in 2026 (up 4pp in a week)'; 'Rising Treasury yields are carving a sharp divide in the market.' The persisted evidence shows the OPPOSITE of an easing cycle -- rate-cut odds falling, hike odds rising.
rules.trigger_rationale: This is a well-evidenced ABSENT, not merely a lack of data: affirmative, quantified contrary evidence (rising hike odds, falling cut odds) was found. One conditional/explanatory statement exists ('falling rates would tend to support valuations') but it describes the RELATIONSHIP, not evidence that rates ARE currently falling.

rules.evidence_condition: Current macro evidence supports liquidity expansion, liquidity release, or broad risk-appetite transmission.
rules.evidence_summary: The only claims tagged 'Liquidity Expansion' are actually framed around LOW RECESSION RISK supporting risk appetite ('This low recession risk supports the equity risk appetite that benefits QQQ's growth-heavy composition'), not direct liquidity-specific evidence (money supply, reserves, credit conditions easing per A003's own core thesis). One generic mention: 'QQQ is a high-beta play on... liquidity conditions' (no directional data).
rules.trigger_rationale: Relevant evidence exists but is indirect -- it evidences low recession risk supporting risk appetite generally, not A003's specific liquidity-expansion mechanism (money supply/reserves/credit conditions). Too ambiguous to call PRESENT or ABSENT reliably.

rules.evidence_condition: Current QQQ/market-relevant evidence supports valuation compression or richly-valued-asset downside risk.
rules.evidence_summary: 'Any disappointment in aggregate earnings growth among mega-cap constituents, or a rise in discount rates, could trigger multiple compression' (fundamental_agent, explicitly ETF-aggregate-framed); 'Valuation Risk / Priced-for-Perfection: Software names... being punished even on beats, signaling multiple compression risk in richly valued growth'; 'rate-driven multiple compression in long-duration software/growth names.'
rules.trigger_rationale: Extensive, explicitly ETF-constituent-aggregate-framed valuation-risk evidence from a Primary fundamental source plus repeated news-agent corroboration.

rules.evidence_condition: Current macro evidence supports recession risk or an earnings-downturn transmission channel.
rules.evidence_summary: 'Only 6% probability of US recession by end of 2026' (down 1pp on the week); 'This low recession risk supports the equity risk appetite that benefits QQQ'; 'resilient labor market... AI capex cycle... no signs of slowing.' The persisted evidence affirmatively shows LOW, not elevated, recession risk.
rules.trigger_rationale: Well-evidenced ABSENT: the corpus contains explicit, quantified evidence that recession risk is low and receding, which is the opposite of A501's defining condition.

rules.evidence_condition: Current ETF/mega-cap/AI-market narrative or momentum evidence supports a reflexive narrative structure.
rules.evidence_summary: 'The AI narrative remains the dominant force in QQQ's largest holdings'; 'This is the single dominant macro narrative and directly hits QQQ's high-multiple tech holdings'; 'the fund [is] a high-conviction, high-beta expression of the AI/semiconductor... narrative.' (Unrelated MACD/RSI technical price-momentum matches were excluded as a different concept from narrative/attention momentum.)
rules.trigger_rationale: Repeated, explicit narrative-dominance language directly and appropriately framed at the ETF/constituent-aggregate level.

rules.evidence_condition: Whether STRONG current evidence could defensibly support an ETF-level aggregate fundamental/revenue transmission interpretation for A301.
rules.evidence_summary: 'The elevated PE ratio reflects expectations of continued revenue growth and earnings expansion among constituents' (Revenue Growth-tagged, ETF-appropriately framed); 'Monitor concentration leaders: track the fundamental health (revenue growth, AI demand, datacenter capex) of the largest constituents.' Only 2 claims found; both are forward-looking/expectational framing rather than concrete realized aggregate revenue data.
rules.trigger_rationale: qqq_a301_strong_etf_level_evidence = UNCERTAIN. Genuine, appropriately-ETF-framed evidence exists (not a single-company earnings claim, but constituent-aggregate framing) but is thin and largely expectational rather than concretely STRONG. Not turned into PRESENT to make later acceptance easier, per instruction.

rules.evidence_condition: Current SNDK-specific evidence supports semiconductor/storage-cycle conditions (inventory, orders, ASP, capex, demand recovery/deterioration).
rules.evidence_summary: 'The institutional news flow... is decisively bullish on SNDK, with a strong AI-memory narrative dominating' (entities=[SNDK,AI]); '$95 billion AI-server backlog fueling memory demand' (factors=[AI Demand, Semiconductor Cycle]); 'NAND pricing cycle... still accelerating'; 'memory shortages are real and will persist for years' (IT-leader sourced).
rules.trigger_rationale: Extensive, dated, SNDK-entity-tagged evidence of an active memory/storage pricing and demand cycle -- directly matching A201's own core thesis (inventory/pricing/demand-cycle dynamics), not merely industry membership.

rules.evidence_condition: Whether STRONG SNDK-specific evidence exists for A101 (material AI training/compute-demand expansion) and A102 (material inference-side compute demand) directly relevant to SNDK.
rules.evidence_summary: sndk_a101_strong_ai_evidence = ABSENT: extensive 'AI demand' language exists ('$95B AI-server backlog fueling MEMORY demand', 'AI model releases... driving STORAGE demand') but it consistently describes AI-driven STORAGE/MEMORY demand -- a distinct, adjacent mechanism from A101's own core thesis (accelerator/GPU/training-compute demand, per taxonomy trigger/confirmation signals). No evidence found of SNDK providing or benefiting from accelerator/training-compute demand itself. sndk_a102_strong_inference_evidence = ABSENT: only 1 matching claim, from bull_researcher (argumentative debate source, not Primary company-specific evidence), thin and conflated with several other claims -- not credible/strong standalone evidence of inference-side compute demand.
rules.trigger_rationale: This is exactly the discrimination the negative control is designed to make: SNDK has real, strong AI-ADJACENT (storage-demand) evidence, but that is a DIFFERENT mechanism from A101's accelerator/training thesis or A102's inference thesis. Classified ABSENT for both, not merely 'no evidence' -- real evidence exists but for a distinguishable, non-matching mechanism. Evidence_strength MODERATE reflects that this is a substantive, reasoned discrimination rather than a simple absence of any AI-related content.

rules.concept: Enterprise AI / cloud AI expansion (conditional mapping only)
rules.evidence_condition: Current MSFT-specific evidence describes AI training/cloud-AI demand growth genuinely attributable to MSFT.
rules.evidence_summary: 'This is a direct catalyst for Azure AI demand'; 'OpenAI's competitive position directly drives Azure AI consumption'; 'AI capex payoff debate -- institutions debate whether MSFT's massive AI spending will pay off.'
rules.trigger_rationale: Genuine Azure-AI-demand evidence exists and is MSFT-attributed, though entangled with the capex-payoff debate framing rather than pure demand-growth language -- MODERATE rather than STRONG.

rules.evidence_condition: Current MSFT-specific evidence explicitly describes inference workloads/compute demand, serving AI applications/models, agent/application inference, or inference-side compute consumption.
rules.evidence_summary: 'The massive capex buildout signals Microsoft's commitment to expanding Azure capacity to meet AI training AND INFERENCE demand' (factors=[Inference Demand]); 'Microsoft's AI products (Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Azure AI services) are DRIVING INFERENCE DEMAND and enterprise adoption'; 'It is driving Inference Demand through products like Microsoft 365 Copilot and Azure AI services, which in turn is driving Revenue Growth.'
rules.trigger_rationale: Multiple claims (fundamental_agent Primary source, bull_researcher, bear_researcher) explicitly name 'inference demand' as the mechanism, directly tied to named MSFT products (Copilot, Azure AI services) -- satisfies the DIRECT trigger's explicit-mechanism requirement.

rules.evidence_condition: Current MSFT-specific evidence describes only broader enterprise AI adoption/Copilot usage/generic AI demand WITHOUT clearly engaging the inference mechanism.
rules.evidence_summary: No claim was found describing MSFT Copilot/enterprise-AI adoption in isolation from the inference-mechanism language already captured by MSFT-A102-DIRECT-INFERENCE-TRIGGER -- the corpus's Copilot-related content consistently and explicitly invokes 'inference demand' rather than remaining generic.
rules.trigger_rationale: Cannot cleanly disentangle a distinct 'generic adoption only, no inference language' evidence pool from the direct-trigger claims already found -- the two categories are not cleanly separable in this corpus. Reported as UNCERTAIN rather than forcing a PRESENT or ABSENT that the evidence does not clearly support, per instruction not to collapse the two trigger classes into one judgment.

rules.concept: AI capex burden (not automatically a valuation-risk Alpha)
rules.evidence_condition: Current MSFT-specific evidence connects AI/cloud capex burden to a downstream financial-pressure channel.
rules.evidence_summary: capex_present = PRESENT: extensive capex discussion ('AI capex payoff debate', 'massive AI spending', 'capex has more than doubled'). capex_downside_linkage_present = PRESENT: 'free cash flow has begun to decline ($67.0B vs $71.6B prior year) due to the capex acceleration' (fundamental_agent, Primary, concrete FCF figures); 'If AI demand does not materialize at the pace expected, this could pressure margins and free cash flow'; bear_researcher: 'The AI CapEx is crushing free cash flow.'
rules.trigger_rationale: Both sub-conditions independently confirmed present with concrete, quantified, Primary-sourced evidence -- capex is explicitly and concretely linked to a real FCF decline, not asserted from capex volume alone.

rules.concept: AI/infrastructure demand -> semiconductor/foundry demand -> TSM-specific company impact
rules.evidence_condition: Current evidence supports at least one leg of the confirmed canonical transmission chain (A101->A201->A301), with A103 as optional supporting context only.
rules.evidence_summary: A101 (upstream AI demand): PRESENT/STRONG -- '$1.3 Trillion in Projected Data Center Spending in 2027'; 'TSM's fate is tightly coupled to the AI CapEx cycle.' A201 (foundry/semiconductor-cycle): PRESENT/STRONG -- 'TSM is framed as the foundry "everything else depends on"'; 'benefiting regardless of which chip designer wins'; institutional accumulation cited. A301 (company revenue): PRESENT/STRONG -- 'two consecutive years of >30% revenue growth (2024 and 2025), driven by the AI infrastructure buildout'; 'revenue growth acceleration... to a 36% YoY pace in Q2 2026... directly tied to AI chip demand' (concrete, quantified, fundamental_agent Primary source). A103 (optional supporting): PRESENT -- '$1.3T data center spending', 'TSM sits at the center of the AI infrastructure buildout' (contextual only, not load-bearing).
rules.trigger_rationale: All three core legs of the confirmed canonical chain (A101, A201, A301) are independently PRESENT with strong, concrete, TSM-specific evidence -- this is the most fully-evidenced composite trigger of the six tickers. A103 present only as optional supporting context, consistent with its OPTIONAL_SUPPORTING_ALPHA status (never treated as proof of a structural A103->A201 edge).

rules.evidence_condition: Current AMD-specific evidence supports AI/semiconductor growth (A101 and/or A301) AND valuation-risk evidence (A304) coexisting.
rules.evidence_summary: Growth side: PRESENT/STRONG -- 'strong demand for AMD's AI accelerators and server CPUs' (Instinct MI300/MI350/MI400 series named); '50% YoY revenue growth in the latest quarter with continued sequential acceleration' (fundamental_agent, Primary). Valuation-risk side: PRESENT/STRONG -- 'multiple compression could pressure AMD despite strong fundamentals'; 'At 122x trailing earnings, the stock is priced for perfection' (factors=[Valuation Risk]).
rules.trigger_rationale: Both composite legs independently present with concrete, TSM-... err AMD-specific quantified evidence (50% revenue growth; 122x trailing earnings). A201 (industry-wide semiconductor cycle) evidence is thinner/mixed (AMD noted as a 'relative laggard' vs NVDA in some claims) but is only an optional element of this rule's acceptable_alphas -- the primary growth trigger (A101+A301) is independently sufficient.

anti_leakage.statement: Only structured_agent_outputs.json (per-ticker, all six authoritative runs) was read as evidence source in this task, plus the frozen Gold v0.2 contract/manifest and the fresh-run ledger for authority verification. No alpha_activations.json, no structure_graph.json activation block, no alpha_matches.json matched_alpha field, no conflicts.json, and no final acceptance/PASS-FAIL artifact was opened.
